page.title: Virtual Events Production: Decisions, Costs, and Workflows
page.description: Learn what to decide first, typical costs, timelines, staffing, deliverables, rehearsal steps, and tool stacks for virtual and hybrid event production.
page.h1: Virtual events production: what to decide, budget, and run
page.definition: Virtual events production is the end-to-end service that turns a platform licence into a live show, covering run of show, speaker rehearsals, branded graphics, live switching, Q&A moderation, backup streaming, and edited recordings.
page.quick_answer: Lock the platform and the production partner before the agenda; budget two thousand five hundred to seven thousand five hundred for a moderated webinar and ten thousand to fifty thousand plus for a summit; allow three to four weeks for a webinar and six to eight weeks for a conference.

sections.h2: What platform and production choices come first?

blocks.p: The platform is software; production is the crew, cameras, encoder, run of show, and backup stream. You buy both separately.

head: Purchase
What you get

rows: Streaming studio, registration, analytics, attendee UI
Show caller, speaker manager, platform operator, backup stream, edited clips

sections.h2: How much does virtual event production cost?

blocks.p: Pricing follows two published ranges from West Peek Productions, which produces events on the platform you choose and does not sell software.

ul: Moderated webinars: two thousand five hundred to seven thousand five hundred per production
Executive summits, online conferences, and hybrid productions: ten thousand to fifty thousand and above
Cost varies with speaker count, hybrid venues, simultaneous tracks, and translation

sections.h2: What timeline and staffing do you need?

blocks.p: Lead time and crew size scale with complexity; a simple webinar moves faster than a multi-track summit.

ul: Webinar: three to four weeks from brief to live; one producer can run it
Summit or online conference: six to eight weeks; needs show caller, speaker manager, moderator, and platform operator
Hybrid conference: lock venue AV and platform six to eight weeks out before the agenda is final

sections.h2: What deliverables should a production partner provide?

blocks.p: A complete production package covers pre-show, live, and post-show assets so the event runs without gaps.

ul: Run of show and speaker brief with rehearsal
Branded slide template and lower thirds
Backup stream on a second encoder
Edited recording and highlight clips delivered within twenty-four to forty-eight hours

sections.h2: How do you run rehearsals and manage the live day?

blocks.p: Two checkpoints protect the broadcast: a full rehearsal on the real platform and a final technical check.

ol: Schedule one full rehearsal on the actual platform two to five days before the event
Run every speaker through cues, transitions, and Q&A flow
Conduct a sixty-minute technical check sixty minutes before going live
Verify backup stream, audio levels, and lower-third triggers
Go live with show caller directing the platform operator

faq.q: How early should I book production for a summit?
faq.a: Reserve a production partner six to eight weeks before the event date; this locks crew, rehearsal slots, and backup encoder availability before the agenda is final.

faq.q: Can I use my existing webinar license with a production team?
faq.a: Yes. Production runs on the platform you already use such as Zoom Webinars, Microsoft Teams, ON24, or StreamYard; the crew joins as panelists and controls the broadcast.

faq.q: What happens if the stream fails during the event?
faq.a: A backup stream on a second encoder runs in parallel; the show caller switches viewers to the backup within seconds while the primary encoder recovers.

faq.q: How fast do I get the recording and clips?
faq.a: Edited recordings and highlight clips are delivered within twenty-four to forty-eight hours so you can publish while attendees still remember the event.
